glosses: to join, to unite, to integrate (to form into one whole)

examples.text: Zespolił ze sobą części za pomocą kleju.

glosses: To include as a constituent part or functionality.

examples.text: They were keen to integrate their new skills into the performance.
All of Peter Schickele's music, both straight and comedic are integrated side by side in this chapter.

glosses: To join a group or an environment harmoniously; to make oneself fit in.

examples.text: The refugees integrated well into the community.
The eco-friendly building integrates with the forest around it.

glosses: To form into one whole; to make entire; to complete; to renew; to restore; to perfect.

examples.text: Virtually free of pain, she has integrated the broken pieces of her life, is a loving and loved wife and mother, and is back at her job.

glosses: To give the sum or total of a varying quantity over an interval such as a period of time or an area.

examples.text: Data gathered at each remote site include sulphur dioxide in parts per million, a five-minute integrated wind direction to the nearest degree and a five-minute integrated wind speed to the nearest one-tenth knot.

glosses: To subject to the operation of integration; to find the integral of an equation.

examples.text: As Example 9 indicates, we can integrate sinⁿ x if we know how to integrate sinⁿ⁻² x.

glosses: To desegregate, as a school or neighborhood.

examples.text: President Eisenhower had to call out the National Guard to integrate Little Rock Central High School.

glosses: To combine compatible elements in order to incorporate them.
Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see bring, together.

examples.text: Although third-rail operation in the region dates back more than a century, it was in the 1970s that tunnels under Liverpool's city centre opened to bring together previously disparate routes.

glosses: To cause people to do something together; to bring about togetherness.

examples.text: The new government will try to unite the various factions.
I hope this song can unite people from all different cultures.
If we want to win, we will need to unite.

glosses: A British gold coin worth 20 shillings, first produced during the reign of King James I, and bearing a legend indicating the king's intention of uniting the kingdoms of England and Scotland.

examples.text: Occasionally Scots and Irish coins are also found. The gold hoards consist entirely of crown gold unites, half unites and quarter unites from the reigns of James I and Charles I.
